chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no cutting off [of the hand] for theft involving fruit, nor for kathar; and kathar is the pith of the date-palm.”

key_terms.ثَمَرٍ: fruit; produce that is excluded here from the hadd punishment
key_terms.قَطْعَ: amputation as the prescribed hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.كَثَرٍ: kathar; a type of date-palm substance excluded from the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for theft apply to stealing fruit or parts of a date-palm?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply in cases involving stolen fruit or kathar. It also clarifies the meaning of kathar as the pith of the date-palm, indicating a specific exclusion within theft rulings.
